name: [Portal] Partner websites: static microsites vs WordPress-on-API, effort and vendor
description:
### Summary

This analysis decides how the three public partner websites (partneri.shoptet.cz for CZ, SK and HU) will get medailonek data once CRM becomes the master record and the Partner Portal lets partners edit their own profiles. Two options are on the table: rebuild the sites as static microsites on the stack Shoptet already uses, fed by the new read API, or keep the existing WordPress installations and connect them to that API. The deliverable is a written recommendation with an inventory of what the current sites do, an architecture sketch and effort range for each option, a redirect and SEO plan for existing partner URLs, a list of what the read API must provide, the impact on the April 2027 MVP target, and a fallback trigger. It involves the microsites vendor and Partnership. It produces no code; the implementation tasks are created from its decision.

### Why?

The three partner websites (CZ/SK/HU) must read medailonky from the CRM API instead of their own WordPress content, otherwise portal edits never reach the public. The MVP scope keeps two options open (wiki Q5): rebuild the sites as static microsites on the stack we already use, fed by the API (preferred), or keep WordPress and connect it to the API. The choice drives effort, vendor involvement and whether April 2027 holds. A one-month slip is acceptable; WordPress-on-API is the fallback if April is at risk. This analysis produces the decision input; implementation is a separate task.

### What?

A written recommendation covering both options for all three sites: what each needs (build pipeline, hosting, redirects and SEO for existing URLs, contact forms, filters by category and region, i18n), effort per option with the vendor's input, dependency on the read API contract (), risk to the April target, and a go/no-go proposal. Out of scope: design work, content rewriting, any rebuild of doplnky.shoptet.cz.

### Acceptance Criteria

Inventory per site of what WordPress does beyond listing medailonky (pages, forms, filters, SEO, analytics), marked keep / drop

Option A (static microsites on API) and option B (WordPress on API) each with an architecture sketch, work breakdown and effort range; vendor consulted and quoted for the parts they would deliver

Redirect and SEO plan for existing partner URLs (per-site slugs vs. one global slug) covered in both options

Explicit list of what the read API must provide for each option; gaps fed back into 

Timeline impact on April 2027 per option, with a fallback trigger ("switch to B if A is not on track by <date>")

Recommendation reviewed with Partnership and the microsites vendor; decision recorded here and implementation task(s) created from it

### Open questions

- Wiki Q5: who owns hosting and build for the static stack, and does the vendor have capacity in Q1 2027?
- Do the SK and HU sites share the CZ structure, or diverge?
- Does another Shoptet static-site project already use the same stack we could reuse (build, hosting, deploy)?

### Technical notes

_Generated by Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-09-16_

- The WordPress sites have no code in the monorepo; they are external.
- Whatever the option, these monorepo references to partneri.shoptet.cz must keep working: marketing links in `cms/controllers/ShoptetFooterController.php` and storefront templates; CORS allow-list `cms/packages/Cors/Helper/CorsHeaders.php`; referrer list `cms/packages/Statistics/Helper/InternalStatsHelper.php`.
- Per-site slugs vs. one global `partner.slug` (UNIQUE in `st_crm.partner`) is the main data constraint for redirects; see also .
